questions.question: What is the main purpose of Kubernetes?

options.text: To replace application source code.
To automate the deployment, scaling and management of containerized applications.
To act as a programming language.
To guarantee that applications contain no bugs.

questions.explanation: Kubernetes manages containerized workloads, helping automate deployment, scaling and recovery. Application development and testing are still necessary.

questions.question: What is a node in a Kubernetes cluster?

options.text: A physical or virtual machine that can run Pods.
A single environment variable.
A folder containing only application images.
A user's browser session.

questions.explanation: A node is a machine in the cluster. Its components allow it to run Pods and communicate with the Kubernetes control plane.

questions.question: What is a Pod?

options.text: An entire cloud region.
A replacement for the cluster control plane.
A file that stores every cluster log.
The smallest deployable computing unit in Kubernetes, containing one or more containers.

questions.explanation: A Pod contains one or more containers that are scheduled together and share networking and storage resources configured for the Pod.

questions.question: What does the Kubernetes scheduler do?

options.text: Write application code automatically.
Build every container image.
Select a suitable node for a Pod that has not yet been assigned to a node.
Replace all application configuration.

questions.explanation: The scheduler assigns unscheduled Pods to nodes, considering resource requirements, constraints and other scheduling factors.

questions.question: Why use a Deployment for a stateless application?

options.text: To manage the desired number of Pod replicas and support controlled updates.
To guarantee permanent storage inside every container.
To remove the need for container images.
To ensure Pods can never be replaced.

questions.explanation: A Deployment manages ReplicaSets to maintain the desired application replicas and supports updates to the Pod template.

questions.question: A Deployment requests three replicas. One of its Pods is deleted. What does Kubernetes normally attempt to do?

options.text: Permanently reduce the desired replica count to two.
Delete the entire cluster.
Wait for a user to recreate the Pod manually.
Create a replacement Pod to restore the desired replica count.

questions.explanation: The ReplicaSet controller attempts to maintain the requested number of replicas. A replacement Pod can become available if scheduling and startup succeed.

questions.question: Why use a Service to access application Pods?

options.text: It prevents application Pods from ever restarting.
It provides a stable way to reach a changing set of Pods.
It compiles the application source code.
It automatically makes every application publicly accessible.

questions.explanation: A Service provides a stable network abstraction for accessing Pods even as individual Pods are replaced. External exposure depends on the Service type and infrastructure.

questions.question: How does a typical selector-based Service identify the application Pods it should target?

options.text: By choosing Pods with the longest names.
By reading comments in the application code.
By matching its selector against Pod labels.
By selecting every Pod in every namespace.

questions.explanation: A selector-based Service matches Pod labels in its namespace. Kubernetes uses the matching Pods to maintain the Service's endpoints.
